overview.headline: Quicksort partitions around a pivot and sorts recursively

keyPoints.point: Students learn quicksort picks a pivot and recursively sorts partitions of smaller and larger elements.
keyPoints.quote: Pick an element from the array (the pivot), partition the remaining elements into those greater than and less than this pivot

keyPoints.point: Students learn quicksort running time is quadratic in the worst case but typically faster.
keyPoints.quote: Quicksort has running time Θ(n²) in the worst case, but it is typically O(n log n).

keyPoints.point: Students learn selecting good pivots can give a variant with better worst case running time.
keyPoints.quote: Select can be used to always pick good pivots, thus giving a variant with O(n log n) worst-case running time.

keyTerms.gloss: Chosen element used to split remaining elements into greater and smaller groups

keyTerms.gloss: Repeated use of divide and conquer to sort each partition
keyTerms.quote: partition, divide and conquer, recursion, Select, sublinear time algorithm.

keyTerms.gloss: Input pattern with slow running time instead of typically fast running time
